mechanism_narrative: EGFR-INSR forced-proximity via rigid_helix_20 (~30 Å) enables transphosphorylation between EGFR kinase (Y712-979) and INSR kinase (Y1023-1298), with ECD asymmetry of only 110 aa (621 vs 731) favoring productive co-clustering. The biased output strongly activates the GRB2-SHC1-SOS-RAS-MAPK and IRS1-PI3K-AKT axes (shared transphosphorylation adaptors), while sterically excluding PLCG1/PLCG2 docking (large multi-domain phospholipases cannot bridge the ~30 Å intracellular gap imposed by the rigid helix). This produces a transcriptional program that upregulates muscle structural/contractile genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, MYOM2, TAGLN) and downregulates aged-muscle IEGs (EGR1, FOS, JUN) and inflammatory/atrophy markers (IL32, TXNIP, MYF5, MYH9), consistent with the rejuvenating pattern observed in ERBB2+FGFR wins.
